heat.source: NOAA NCEI nClimDiv county monthly minimum temperature

water.source: USDA Census of Agriculture 2022 (NASS Quick Stats) + USGS Estimated Use of Water 2015 county data (usco2015v2.0.xlsx)

loss.source: USDA RMA Summary of Business, Cause of Loss (colsom_YYYY.zip)
loss.premium_note: premium and liability are from rows that carry a loss; not total county premium

sob.source: USDA RMA Summary of Business, state/county/crop/coverage (sobcov_YYYY.zip)

drought.source: U.S. Drought Monitor county statistics API (NDMC/UNL), cumulative area percent, weekly maps since 2000-01-04
drought.note: d2 = weeks with at least 50% of the county's area in D2 or worse; d3 = same for D3 or worse; maps = weekly maps counted

energy.source: EIA Form 860 2025 (Plant and Generator workbooks, Operable and Proposed tabs)
energy.note: MW are nameplate; technology classed on SOLAR / WIND / BATTER in the EIA technology string; rooftop solar under 1 MW is not in Form 860

wells.source: Nebraska DNR registered groundwater wells (gis.ne.gov) + Kansas DWR WIMAS points of diversion (services.kgs.ku.edu)

thesis_test.claim: Counties with warmer July and August nights have gained corn yield more slowly.
thesis_test.window_note: The yield trend is fitted on the published county yields since 2008, a window that holds the 2012 drought and is dominated by genetics and management, so a weak result here does not refute a longer-run heat effect; the decade series on the map is the longer record. Rows marked across all counties compare counties as they sit, and night heat rises to the south along with several other things that move yield, so the verdict reads the within-state rows, where each county is compared only with the other counties of its own state, and their fifths are deviations from the state's mean, not yield gains. That removes the between-state contrast, which is the largest heat contrast in the sample, and it leaves the north-south gradient inside Texas, Kansas and Nebraska in place. The chance column treats counties as independent; neighbouring counties are not, so read it as generous.
thesis_test.verdict: Within a state, counties with warmer nights gained yield faster (r +0.22); that is where the longer season is, not the thesis. The trend of night heat, which is the thesis, shows no relationship the data can vouch for.
